transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because I keep having these nights where I eat an amount of food that honestly scares me. I’ll start with just some leftovers after I finish grading papers, but then... I don't know, I just keep going. I end up going through cereal, crackers, peanut butter, and even whatever snacks I packed for my classroom. It's just a really large amount of food, and I knew I needed to come talk to someone about it.
During these episodes when you're eating large amounts of food, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating, even if you wanted to?

Yeah, that is exactly how it is. Once I start... it's like I have no control over it at all. It literally feels like the reasonable, teacher part of me is just watching from the outside, saying, "Joan, stop." But I just can't. My hands keep opening things and putting food in my mouth, over and over, and I don't stop until I’m just painfully full.

After these episodes where you eat so much, do you do anything to try to undo it or prevent weight gain—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising a lot, or restricting food the next day?

Yeah, I do. I don't make myself throw up or use laxatives or anything like that, but... well, after one of those nights, I’ll just tell myself I’m not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school the next day. I just skip them completely. 

And then I make sure to exercise a lot to make up for it. I’ll stay out on the running trail for hours, or I'll force myself to do extra yoga, even when I’m just... shaky and completely exhausted from not eating. I just feel like I have to undo what I did the night before.
On average, how many days per week would you say you're doing these restriction and exercise behaviors to make up for the binge eating episodes?

Well, for the past few months... there has rarely been a week without at least one night where I eat far more than I meant to. And then, you know, the next day I immediately try to make up for it by not eating at school, or pushing myself through a long walk or extra yoga. So it's happening at least once a week, if not more.
How long has this pattern of binge eating episodes been going on—are we talking weeks, months, or longer?
I'd say it's been going on for about four months now. Yeah, right around four months. It started right around the time I took on the literacy lead responsibilities at my school.

I want to make sure I have this right—you mentioned you don't make yourself vomit or use laxatives. Has that ever been something you've done, even once or twice, to try to get rid of food after a binge episode?

No, I've never done that. Not even once or twice. I've just never... I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything like that. I just stick to skipping meals and the exercise to try to deal with it.
When you say at least once a week, can you give me a more specific number? On average, how many binge eating episodes would you say you're having per week right now?

I'm honestly not sure of an exact number. I haven't really been keeping a strict count or writing it down. It just... it feels like it happens a lot. 

Some weeks it seems like it's almost every day, or even multiple times a day if things are really stressful with my classes. But an exact average per week? I just don't know. They all kind of blur together at this point.
I know it's hard to be exact, but thinking back over the past month or so, would you say these binge eating episodes are happening roughly twice a week or more, or less than that?

Oh, it's definitely more than twice a week. Um... yeah, way more. Since it happens almost every day, especially lately, it's... it's well over two times. I just don't have a specific number to give you, but it's absolutely more than that.

You mentioned you don't purge or use laxatives, but I want to ask about diet pills or diuretics—have you ever taken water pills, diet pills, or any other medications to try to lose weight or get rid of the food after a binge episode?

No, I haven't taken any of those either. I don't use water pills or diet pills, or any other kind of medication for that. Like I said earlier, I really just rely on skipping meals and working out a lot to try to fix it after it happens. But no, no pills.
I want to circle back on something—I know you said you don't make yourself vomit now, but have you ever tried purging by vomiting at any point during these four months, even just once or a few times?

No, I've never tried making myself throw up. Not even once. I know some people do that, but I've never done it, not even when things were really bad over the last few months. It's just the fasting and the exercise for me.
